introduction: All 125 observations carrying our four project fields were re-reviewed. These close-ups were chosen to show the range within categories and the boundaries between them. “Pigment variation” is a visual score of the photographed tissue; it does not measure chemical pigment.

traits.label: Petal Color
traits.summary: Judge the broad upper petal tissue between the veins. Exclude the yellow/orange throat, any separate white center ring, and the vein lines themselves. Our Figure 1 key is Pink A–F, Purple G–H, and White I–P.

categories.definition: White or near-white interveinal tissue, including a cool cast. Colored veins alone do not make a flower Pink or Purple.

examples.alt: An open white flower with very faint petal lines and a yellow-green center.
examples.title: White with very faint veins
examples.caption: The broad tissue is white and the fine lines are barely visible. Judge the petals outside the yellow throat.
examples.attribution: (c) Big Year, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A cool near-white flower with faint veins.
examples.title: Cool near-white still counts as White
examples.caption: The tissue has a cool appearance but remains near-white. This project includes pale cool-looking flowers in White rather than treating every lilac cast as pigment.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A white flower crossed by a bold purple vein network.
examples.title: Purple lines, white background
examples.caption: The purple vein network is strong, but the spaces between its lines are white. This is White color with High vein contrast.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

categories.definition: Rose, magenta, or pale pink-lilac background tissue, matching A–F in our reference key. Saturation alone does not separate Pink from Purple.

examples.alt: A cupped flower with saturated rose-magenta upper petals.
examples.title: Saturated rose and magenta
examples.caption: The broad rose/magenta tissue fits Pink, as do C and D in our Figure 1 key. Its cupped center makes the ring uncertain, but does not erase the visible petal color.
examples.attribution: (c) Amy Frost-Wicks, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A pale rose-lilac flower with a white basal band.
examples.title: Pale pink-lilac
examples.caption: The visible broad tissue is pale rose/lilac and falls in Pink. Soft detail makes some structural traits uncertain; the background color is still discernible.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: An open rose-pink flower surrounding a distinct white basal band.
examples.title: Rose-pink around a white center
examples.caption: The outer petal background is rose-pink. Exclude the white basal band when deciding the flower’s background color.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

categories.definition: Clearly violet background tissue like G and H. The violet must be in the broad tissue, not confined to vein lines.

examples.alt: A violet flower with subtle veins and a white center ring.
examples.title: Violet with subtle veins
examples.caption: Clearly violet tissue occupies the broad parts of the petals. The fine veins are subtle against it, so the color is Purple even with Low vein contrast.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: Violet outer petals around a broad, distinct white basal ring.
examples.title: Violet outside a broad white ring
examples.caption: Use the violet outer tissue for color. The broad white center band is a separately scored ring and does not make this a White flower.
examples.attribution: (c) Eric Duran, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower with visible darker veins and a white basal ring.
examples.title: Violet with visible vein lines
examples.caption: The spaces between the darker lines are themselves violet. Both background pigment and veins are visible; the background establishes Purple.
examples.attribution: (c) Dillon Doss, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

categories.definition: Use this when the visible background remains unresolved between categories or the available view does not provide reliable color evidence.

examples.alt: A pale flower with bold magenta veins whose broad background is uncertain between cool white and pale lilac.
examples.title: Cool white or pale pigmented lilac?
examples.caption: The broad tissue cannot be placed confidently between cool white and pale lilac pigment. Its bold magenta veins can still be scored High independently.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

traits.label: Petal Vein Contrast
traits.summary: At the standard 300-pixel view, judge how strongly vein lines stand out from their immediate petal background. Assess prominence, not vein color, number, or branching.

categories.definition: Lines are faint, subtle, or not visible in an otherwise adequate image. Low does not mean veins are anatomically absent.

examples.alt: A sharply shown white flower with very faint vein lines.
examples.title: At the faint end
examples.caption: Fine lines are barely visible against the white tissue. The clear broad background supports Low rather than an uncertainty caused by blur.
examples.attribution: (c) Big Year, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: An ivory-white flower with pale subtle veins.
examples.title: Pale lines remain subtle
examples.caption: The pale vein lines are visible on close inspection but remain subtle at this standard size. They do not carry the readily visible contrast required for Medium.
examples.attribution: (c) Dan Blanchard, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower whose fine veins remain subtle against the colored tissue.
examples.title: Low on colored petals
examples.caption: Fine veins blend into the saturated violet background. A deeply colored flower can still have Low vein contrast.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

categories.definition: Veins are readily visible but remain secondary to the broad petal background. Figure 1 A, F, and H define this class.

examples.alt: A white flower with readily visible pink vein lines.
examples.title: Visible pink lines on white
examples.caption: Pink vein lines are easy to see, but the pale background still leads the overall impression. Re-review placed this in Medium rather than High.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower with visible but secondary darker vein lines.
examples.title: Visible lines on violet
examples.caption: The darker lines stand out from nearby violet tissue without dominating the flower. Contrast is assessed against the local background.
examples.attribution: (c) Dillon Doss, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A pale pink-lilac flower with visible vein lines and a narrow white basal band.
examples.title: Lines within pale pink-lilac
examples.caption: The lines are readily visible in the pink-lilac tissue but remain secondary. Broad changes in the background are assessed separately as pigment variation.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

categories.definition: A strongly contrasting vein network is a dominant visual feature across the visible petals. Compare Figure 1 O and P.

examples.alt: A white flower with a dominant branching purple vein network.
examples.title: A dominant purple network
examples.caption: The bold purple network is a leading feature of the white petals. The white spaces between lines still establish White petal color.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A white flower with bold contrasting colored vein lines across the petals.
examples.title: Strong lines across the petals
examples.caption: The contrasting network draws attention across the flower at the standard size. This is prominence across broad visible petals, not simply the presence of a few colored lines.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: An open white flower with a dark prominent vein network.
examples.title: Dark network on white tissue
examples.caption: Dark lines dominate the visible white petals. The ridges, shadows, and colored lines do not by themselves establish pigment variation in the broad tissue.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

categories.definition: Blur, inadequate source detail, glare, or clipped highlights prevent a reliable comparison between lines and background.

examples.alt: A defocused white flower whose vein detail is not resolved.
examples.title: Blur is not Low contrast
examples.caption: The white background is discernible, but defocus removes the detail needed to judge vein prominence. Do not turn missing detail into Low.
examples.attribution: (c) Trevor Harding, some rights reserved (CC BY)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A white flower with clipped highlights and visible dark lines.
examples.title: Highlights distort the comparison
examples.caption: Clipped bright tissue may exaggerate the contrast of surviving dark lines. The apparent line strength cannot be scored reliably.
examples.attribution: (c) Levin Pratte, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

traits.label: White Center Ring
traits.summary: Inspect the transition immediately outside the yellow/orange throat on at least three visible petal bases. Judge whether a separate pale band is absent, faint, or clearly bounded against the outer tissue.

categories.definition: Colored petal tissue reaches the throat without an intervening pale or white band. The bases must be exposed well enough to establish absence.

examples.alt: A violet flower whose exposed colored petal bases reach the throat without a white ring.
examples.title: Colored tissue reaches the throat
examples.caption: The visible violet background continues to the throat without a distinct intervening pale band. Subtle light and dark areas farther out are scored as variation instead.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower with colored bases reaching the yellow throat and modest paler areas farther along the petals.
examples.title: Paler middles do not make a ring
examples.caption: Colored tissue reaches the yellow throat on the visible bases. The paler areas farther along the petals belong to Low variation, not a separate basal ring.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

categories.definition: A weak pale band is visible just outside the throat but blends softly into the outer colored tissue. Faint describes a visible feature, not uncertain evidence.
categories.note: This is the only licensed Faint example selected from the 125 reviewed observations. Observation 294114815 remains a linked working comparison in the protocol; its all-rights-reserved photo is not reproduced here.

examples.alt: A violet flower with a weak pale basal band blending softly into the outer tissue.
examples.title: A weak, softly blended band
examples.caption: A pale basal band is visible, but its boundary blends into the surrounding violet tissue. Its weak separation supports Faint rather than Clear.
examples.attribution: (c) Trevor Van Loon, some rights reserved (CC BY)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

categories.definition: A distinct white band separates the throat from colored outer tissue on at least three petals. Width alone does not determine the category: a narrow but distinct band can be Clear.

examples.alt: A violet flower with a broad white basal ring and a clearly defined outer boundary.
examples.title: Broad and clearly bounded
examples.caption: The large white basal region has a distinct outer boundary against violet tissue. Its size is striking, but it remains a center ring and is excluded from pigment variation.
examples.attribution: (c) Eric Duran, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower with a distinct white band outside its yellow throat.
examples.title: A distinct band outside the throat
examples.caption: The white band is clearly separate from both the yellow throat and violet outer tissue. Vein lines crossing the petals do not remove that distinction.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A rose-pink flower with a distinct white ring around the throat.
examples.title: A white band against rose-pink
examples.caption: The white basal band stands apart from the rose-pink outer tissue across the visible petal bases. The background color of the flower does not change the ring rule.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

categories.definition: Use this for a hidden or unresolved transition, or for white petals with no distinguishable outer boundary for a separate ring. White petals are not automatically an absent ring.

examples.alt: A cupped magenta flower whose oblique center may hide a white basal band.
examples.title: A cupped center can hide a band
examples.caption: The oblique, cupped center may conceal a pale circle. The project owner corrected this to Cannot be determined; a partly hidden band cannot establish Absent.
examples.attribution: (c) Amy Frost-Wicks, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A white flower with no distinguishable outer boundary for a separate white center ring.
examples.title: White tissue has no separate boundary
examples.caption: The petals are white, so no separate outer ring boundary can be identified. This is insufficient evidence for Absent, Faint, or Clear.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

traits.label: Petal Pigment Variation
traits.summary: Look for repeated changes in pigment intensity within the broad background of a petal. Exclude the throat, narrow veins, a separate white center ring, shadows, glare, folds, and damage.

categories.definition: The broad background is nearly uniform after the exclusions above. Both pale and deeply colored flowers can be None; a center ring alone does not increase variation.

examples.alt: A magenta flower with nearly uniform broad petal color.
examples.title: Nearly uniform pink
examples.caption: The broad pink tissue is nearly uniform. Folds and small flecks do not form a repeated broad pigment gradient.
examples.attribution: (c) Amy Frost-Wicks, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower with uniform colored tissue outside a distinct white basal ring.
examples.title: Nearly uniform violet
examples.caption: The colored background is approximately uniform once the separate white basal ring is excluded. A ring is not a pale middle zone within the colored petal.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A white flower with approximately uniform tissue outside the yellow center and fine veins.
examples.title: Nearly uniform white
examples.caption: The white tissue is approximately uniform outside the throat and fine veins. Neither the yellow center nor faint colored lines establishes broad variation.
examples.attribution: (c) Big Year, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower with nearly uniform outer tissue and a large separate white center ring.
examples.title: A broad ring is still excluded
examples.caption: The violet outer tissue is nearly uniform. The large, separately bounded white center ring is excluded from this trait, so it does not push the score to Low or High.
examples.attribution: (c) Eric Duran, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

categories.definition: A subtle but repeatable gradient or modest light/dark difference occurs across the broad tissue, without strongly separated pale and dark zones. An F-like near-white middle is not required.
categories.note: The first two photographs are the project owner’s Low anchors. Compare the broad tissue rather than only the flower’s overall hue.

examples.alt: A violet flower with modest broad paling in the petal middles and stronger pigment elsewhere.
examples.title: Owner’s anchor: paler middle regions
examples.caption: The project owner assigns Low here. Broad middle regions are paler than other petal regions beyond the narrow veins; the modest difference is enough even without sharply separated zones.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower showing modest lighter and darker background regions within the petals.
examples.title: Owner’s anchor: modest broad variation
examples.caption: The project owner assigns Low here. Modest lighter and darker regions occur within the colored petals, beyond the narrow vein lines and faint basal ring.
examples.attribution: (c) Trevor Van Loon, some rights reserved (CC BY)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A violet flower with a modest repeated gradient toward stronger pink-purple outer regions.
examples.title: A more noticeable gradient, still Low
examples.caption: The repeated gradient toward stronger pink-purple outer regions is more noticeable, but the tissue does not form the strongly separated pale and dark zones of Figure 1 F.
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

categories.definition: Clearly distinct pale and dark broad background regions occur across the petals, as in Figure 1 F: pink toward the base, a nearly white middle, and deeper pink near the margins.
categories.note: No confident High example was found among the 125 reviewed observations. Figure 1 F remains the reference. Dark veins, stronger overall saturation, and a separate white center ring are not sufficient.

categories.definition: Use this when broad light/dark changes cannot be separated from illumination or image quality, or the boundary between variation categories remains unresolved.

examples.alt: A violet flower with glare and shadows across its petals.
examples.title: Glare and shadow overlap the tissue
examples.caption: Direct glare and shadows change the apparent intensity across the petals. The available image cannot establish whether a broad pigment gradient is present.
examples.attribution: (c) Sarah Larsen, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: A white flower with droplets, bright wet glare, and soft focus.
examples.title: Wet glare and soft focus
examples.caption: Bright wet surfaces and defocus prevent reliable comparison of background intensity. Apparent pale patches cannot be assigned to pigment variation.
examples.attribution: (c) Julia Prange, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.

examples.alt: An oblique violet flower with strongly uneven illumination across the petals.
examples.title: Uneven illumination is unresolved
examples.caption: Strong differences in illumination produce broad light and dark areas. They cannot confidently be attributed to pigment, so the score remains Cannot be determined.
examples.attribution: (c) Michael Hawk, some rights reserved (CC BY-NC)
examples.cropNote: Cropped around the focal flower and resized for the scoring view; no color or contrast adjustment. Copied unchanged from the reviewed crop.
